author: ValWood
body:
* **UniProt KeyWord (ID and label):**

UniProtKB-KW:KW-0235  DNA replication

* **Sequences with problematic annotation (ID + gene/protein name):**

UniProtKB: Q10154 (rtf1 https://www.pombase.org/gene/SPAC1D4.09c)

* **Description of issue**

This was once considered to be involved in replication restart, but it is clearly a splicing factor and the replication is indirect as a result of incomplete splciig of rtf1

Tony Carr's lab:
https://elifesciences.org/articles/78554
title: Incorrect UniProt KW mapping:UniProtKB-KW:KW-0235 for Q10154

author: Antonialock
body:
i have curated the paper and updated function and kw. I see you called it a "splicing factor" and annotated to "spliceosomal complex" but the paper says Whether Rtf2 acts directly as a splicing factor or indirectly effects spliceosome function remains to be elucidated

 do you think it's ok to call it a splicing factor despite that?

author: ValWood
body: well, it physically associates with the splicing machinery and results in intron retention, so I think its pretty safe. The only other option is some other aspect of mRNA processing (splicing assembly, but we usually call assembly factors splicing factors too). I'll take another look but it made sense when I curated it.

author: ValWood
body: It could also be RNA surveillance  (of splicing) I guess. Maybe I should be a bit more conservative....
